## Lint review

- Waiting and stopping. Saturated half-open has no time-based recovery with an unreported admission. User work and injected policy can block indefinitely. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06. F-11, step-3 lock-discipline annotation, Q-09.
- Retry bound. No ordinary request retry engine. Execute recovery can attempt failure accounting again when the original accounting panics. F-03, step-8 verification, Q-10.
- External failure. Notification has no returned error or compensation; policy panic can escape and change what the caller sees. F-03, seam-contract sweep, Q-12 and Q-10.
- Cancellation and lifecycle disagreement. A caller exiting or losing its callback leaves the charged generation budget. The old wrapper stays reachable through a retained callback. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06 and Q-17.
- Startup and diagnostics. Constructed Closed and refusal sentinels are explicit. There is no terminal or shutdown operation. A zero receiver has a different initialization and failure path. F-18, step-3 checklist, Q-08.
- Overload. Closed admits freely and stores counters but no pending queue. Half-open exhaustion has ErrTooManyRequests and no timeout. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06. Counter representation is finite, F-05, z3 invariant check, Q-11.
- Synchronized reset. Open expiry admits a fresh local budget; HalfOpen success removes the admission cap. F-10, multi-instance probes, Q-14.
- Dual cleanup and async cancellation isolation. No owned resource destructor or internal async queue. Execute recovery and two-step reports are distinct API forms; duplicate logical completion is reachable through repeated reports and through panic re-accounting. F-14, adversarial trace, Q-03. F-03, step-8 verification, Q-10.
- User-model gap. Admission at equality holds while another call is pending, and the observer can itself refresh state. A State read or earlier outcome can invalidate a later report. F-02, step-4 matrix walk, Q-04. F-05, step-5 lint, Q-02. F-15, adversarial trace, Q-05.
